headline: International Federation on Ageing joins Speak Up for COPD and backs Time to Act Joint Declaration
dek: The IFA said it is part of a coalition of patient, clinical, research, advocacy and industry voices calling for better COPD diagnosis, treatment access and prevention.
body:
The International Federation on Ageing (IFA) said on X that it is part of Speak Up for COPD, an initiative bringing together patient, clinical, research, advocacy and industry voices. The stated shared ambition is better outcomes for people living with, and at risk of, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

The IFA said 480 million people are affected by COPD worldwide, describing the condition as an important part of the global noncommunicable disease (NCD) challenge. It said this is increasingly relevant as populations age and more people live longer with multiple chronic conditions. According to the IFA, addressing chronic respiratory conditions such as COPD is part of helping people maintain their health, function and quality of life as they age, from prevention and risk reduction through to timely diagnosis, appropriate treatment and continuity of care.

Through the Time to Act Joint Declaration, the organisation said it is calling for progress in four areas: timely and accurate diagnosis; equitable access to guideline-recommended treatment; integrated disease management and continuity of care; and prioritisation of COPD prevention and risk reduction.

The IFA said health systems must be ready to prevent, manage and coordinate care for NCDs across the life course, "helping people live not only longer, but healthier lives". It invited the public to follow Speak Up for COPD for updates and to add their support to the Joint Declaration. The post carried the hashtags #SpeakUpForCOPD and #WorldCOPDDay.
key_quote: As populations age, our health systems must be ready to prevent, manage and coordinate care for NCDs across the life course
